chunks: And with this chain, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:
The lowest level of disobedience (to parents) is saying 'uff'; and if God knew of anything lighter than 'uff', He would have forbidden it.

key_terms.أُفٍّ: A word of contempt or sigh of impatience, representing the lightest form of disrespect
key_terms.الْعُقُوقِ: Disobedience or disrespect, specifically towards parents

ai.seo_question: What is the lowest level of disobedience to parents according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifies uttering 'uff'—a sigh of impatience—as the threshold of parental disobedience, using a rhetorical argument that if any act lighter existed, God would have prohibited it, thereby elevating minor gestures to significant sins. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and emotional control in maintaining familial piety, extending the Quranic command of kindness beyond mere physical care to include the tone of voice and inner disposition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-160 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) said,
“The lowest level of being damned by parents is through telling them a word of contempt. If God knew anything lower than this, He would have admonished us against it.”
